construct: Insulin deficiency and hyperosmolality shift potassium out of cells, which may raise serum potassium, while osmotic diuresis, vomiting, and secondary renal losses cause a substantial total-body potassium deficit.

notes: Adult Diabetic Ketoacidosis — StatPearls 2026: serum potassium may be high while intracellular/total-body potassium is depleted; insulin lowers serum potassium.
Hyperglycemic Crises — Endotext current chapter: renal/extrarenal losses reduce total-body K while insulin deficiency/acidosis mask deficit extracellularly.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: DKA causes extracellular potassium shift from insulin deficiency/hyperosmolality while osmotic diuresis and vomiting deplete body stores. Therefore elevated serum potassium can coexist with a substantial total-body deficit before insulin.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: An elevated measured serum potassium could tempt selection of increased body potassium, but DKA causes osmotic renal potassium losses. Current Endotext/StatPearls explicitly distinguish extracellular elevation from depleted total-body stores.
